content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am looking to use a [product_name] (article_no: [article_no]) with a 110VDC power source. Based on the technical specifications, the input voltage for this [product_name] is 115...240 V AC/DC, with a permissible range of 100 ... 253 VDC. Our system's standard voltage is 110VDC, which can fluctuate by ±10% (from 99 to 121 VDC). Is it possible for this [product_name] to function properly with this power supply, considering 99VDC falls just below the permissible range?
Unfortunately, 99VDC is below the specified minimum of 100VDC for this equipment, so there is no assurance it will operate reliably at that voltage.

Hi [user_name], I have tested the [product_name] myself and noticed it can run correctly even with 50VDC as supply voltage. Is there any [document] that clarifies under which circumstances the technical specifications of [product_name] are ensured? Best regards, [user_name]

Greetings! Please keep in mind that specifications represent the conditions under which the manufacturer guarantees proper operation. While the device may work at 50V, [company_name] will not offer a warranty for this scenario. Since 99V is very close but still below the official minimum, you may use it if your application is not critical, but operation is not assured.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing the operational boundaries of [product_name], focusing on its ability to run at voltages slightly below the minimum specified range. Although official documentation does not cover these lower voltages, some users report successful operation even far below the indicated range. However, these cases fall outside guaranteed conditions and warranty, creating uncertainty about how technical data relates to practical use.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek clear, actionable advice on whether [product_name] will be reliable within their desired voltage range, and want reference documentation specifying the exact context and reliability of the official technical data.
